policy: Migrate classes only where relocation genuinely clarifies ownership. Rule 11 and Rule 26 of ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md forbid forcing a class into a module merely because its name contains a domain word, and forbid moving classes just to satisfy a directory diagram.

migrated_in_this_phase.why: Pure Application orchestration over AssetRepositoryInterface. No Models, no Domain, no Http, no service locator. 33 lines, 1 consumer.
Pure Application orchestration over AssetRepositoryInterface. No Models, no Domain, no Http. 23 lines, 2 consumers.

Subscribes to 18 notification events spanning Booking, Media, Partner, Payment, Referral and Profile. Genuinely cross-cutting, so it belongs in Support/Events rather than a domain module. 1 consumer (EventServiceProvider).

why_only_three: The brief lists pricing, availability, booking, payment, refund, settlement and commission calculation as behaviour-change hard stops. Those classes account for 18 of the 45 remaining Services.

Most of the remainder are Eloquent-shaped services; moving them into Application/ without first extracting a persistence port would place Models inside Application and make ownership LESS clear, which Rule 26 prohibits.
The three migrated classes share a property the rest do not: their only dependencies are contracts. That is what made them safe.
A mass relocation of ~25 services would touch most of the 336 files and could not be verified to the required certainty in this phase.

sequenced_plan.gate: Media golden tests (image sizes, storage paths, MimeType edge cases)
existing Reporting query tests; Reporting is already an Application module
FIRST extract a persistence port, THEN move. Moving before extracting makes ownership worse.

explicitly_not_done: No Domain class was created, no value object was extracted, and no Eloquent call was moved. Phase 0.18 in this run is a partial migration with a verified, ordered plan for the remainder.
